subject: Post-demo: NovaPipe schema hardening & decode-fallback strategy

Subject: Post-demo: NovaPipe schema hardening & decode-fallback strategy

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and what we sketched together on the call plus proposed next steps for the engineering deep-dive.

Highlights from the call
- Goal: reliable, predictable structured output for invoice extraction + classification pipeline.
- Constraints you mentioned: max 3k tokens per request, occasional truncated context from upstream, and strict JSON object envelope for downstream parsers.
- Desires: model to emit either the canonical invoice JSON or a small, machine-detectable failure object (so downstream can retry).

What Redwood will validate/propose (attached: novapipe-proposed-schema-v0.json)
1) Canonical JSON Schema (flat invoice + nested line-items) + minimal fallback schema for NACKs.
2) Constrained-decoding patterns: token-level grammar blocking, preferred prefix enforcement for the JSON envelope, and a strict closing-brace guard.
3) Validation + retry rules: syntactic validator (fast), then semantic checks (amounts, date formats). On parse-fail: 2 soft retries with temperature=0.0 / top_p=0.0 and progressive relax of constraints; on repeated failure return standardized failure object.
4) Routing/auth notes: SDK will call embeddings/reranker routes for candidate retrieval before structured generation; auth via service token (we can do short-lived keys via your KMS if required).

Immediate asks for your team
- Confirm whether the downstream consumer can tolerate a failure object {"parse_error": true, "reason": "truncated_input"} or if you prefer a different pattern.
- Share a small sample of raw PDF->OCR output that reproduces the truncation case (even a redacted page is fine).

Next steps / owners
- Tech deep-dive to align on constrained-decoding knobs (Hannah / Karthik) — proposed Mon 16 Feb 10am PT.
- Karthik to prepare a sample SDK call sequence and fallback demonstration (will attach code sample).
- Elena to send sample OCR payloads and any security constraints for auth/KMS.

Attachments: novapipe-proposed-schema-v0.json (initial schema), redwood-sdk-sample-auth.zip (example auth hooks).

Thanks —
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — this looks good. A few clarifications from the engineering side:

- The consumer pipeline can accept a failure object, but ideally it includes a short failure_code and a reference id so we can trace quickly (e.g., {"parse_error":true, "failure_code":"TRUNC_01", "ref_id":"<original_doc_id>"}).
- Token-level blocking: can Redwood enforce a left-brace as the first non-whitespace token? We want to avoid stray text before the JSON.
- What does a \"progressive relax\" look like in practice? If first retry with strict grammar still fails, what are recommended next steps from your end?

I've attached an architecture sketch (novapipe-arch-diagram.pdf) and two redacted OCR samples that show how we sometimes lose header lines. We'll upload more to the Drive link you suggested.

Also from a security standpoint: we need short-lived API keys and audit logs. Can Karthik share the expected auth flow and minimum retention for logs?

Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: NovaPipe schema hardening & decode-fallback strategy

Looping in Marcus and Jasmine on implementation approach. High-level proposal below — prefer to walk through live with NovaPipe.

1) Envelope enforcement (token-level):
- Enforce JSON envelope by checking first non-space token; if not '{' then immediate soft-failure without consuming model quota (fast local filter).
- On model response, run a fast syntactic pass (stack-based brace matcher) — extremely cheap.

2) Constrained decoding strategy (order of operations):
- Primary call: temperature=0, top_p=0.0, logits masking to only allow tokens valid under current partial-JSON prefix (prefix-constrained decoding).
- If syntactic failure -> Retry #1: same settings but with allow-list expansion for whitespace/newline tokens and a limited set of punctuation.
- Retry #2: expand to temperature=0.1 and top_p=0.9 with small length penalty to encourage closure; still enforce prefix grammar but allow a larger token set.
- If still fails: return standardized failure object (include failure_code, short model debug info, and a deterministic checksum of the input for tracing).

3) Semantic validation & reranker:
- After a syntactically valid JSON, run schema-based checks (field types, date regex, sum checks for line items).
- If semantic mismatch, attempt a semantic-correction pass that asks the model to correct only the offending fields (minimal prompt + constrained tokens). If correction cannot be validated, mark parse_failure.

4) Observability & audit:
- Emit per-request traces (model variant, token count, retries) into the Console. We can point to a RBAC'ed link for NovaPipe.

Notes on auth/logging: short-lived service tokens are straightforward: we can mint scoped tokens via your KMS (we support rotating keys and audit hooks). I can prepare the SDK snippet and an auth flow diagram.

I'll draft a demo script for the deep-dive that walks through the three failure classes (pre-envelop, syntactic, semantic) with live retries. Marcus will scope the compute/cost impact of multiple retries.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
